question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
n=100,
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =0\cdot 0.2+5\cdot 0.4+10\cdot 0.2+20\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0+2+2+4 \\  & =8,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =({0}^{2}\cdot 0.2+{5}^{2}\cdot 0.4+{10}^{2}\cdot 0.2+{20}^{2}\cdot 0.2)-{8}^{2} \\  & =(0+10+20+80)-64 \\  & =46.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(8,\frac{46}{100}) \\  & ∼N(8,0.46).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<7).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<7) & ≈P(Z<\frac{7-8}{\sqrt{0.46}}) \\  & =P(Z<-1.47) \\  & =Φ(-1.47).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.47)=0.0708.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<7) & =Φ(-1.47) \\  & =0.0708.\end{aligned}
$$
